Hi Alice — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below; I'm pulling the subprocessor matrix and SOC2 snapshot and will attach them. If any of these need to go into an NDA/PROC flow we can route to legal, but for now this is prospect-level evidence.

Summary (short):
- Execution footprint: requests ingress at client-selected region (we honor region param); execution occurs on a matching region allocation when available, otherwise routed to nearest compatible region per policy (we fall back in priority order: same region -> alternative US region -> dedicated APAC/EU pools depending on customer config).
- Hops: Ingress LB -> routing layer -> execution node (GPU pool) -> ephemeral KV/cache (in-memory + encrypted swap) -> short-term request logs (used for billing/observability) -> optional archival (only if customer enables long-term logging).
- Subprocessors: our infra partners (cloud providers) handle physical compute and networking; we use managed observability for metrics/log storage and a dedicated blob store provider for optional archival. Full names in the attached matrix.
- Deletion/TTL: default short retention is 7 days for request traces and 0 days for cached KV unless autosave is enabled. Customers can set retention policy per-project (24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, or disable archive). Permanent deletion request: we remove cached KV entries and request traces within 72 hours; if archival was enabled, we also initiate deletion with the blob provider and provide confirmation.

I'll attach: redwood-subprocessor-matrix-2027.xlsx and SOC2-snapshot-2027.pdf.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Vectra requires zero-cross-border-execution for this PoC (i.e., all execute strictly inside a single named region), or if routing tolerance is acceptable? That determines whether we need to propose a Dedicated or Private deployment for you.

Thanks — Maya

Hi Alice — following up with a couple concrete bullets to add to Maya's note, and clarifications on subprocessors:

- Subprocessors (short list):
  - Cloud compute: MajorCloudProvider (US regions: us-west-2, us-east-1)
  - Observability: ObservoMetrics (logs/metrics retention configurable; SOC2 compliant)
  - Blob archival: ColdStoreCo (used only if customer enables archival)
  - Monitoring/alerting: Pagerline (incident notification only)

- KMS and keys: we use a customer-scoped KMS key for Private and Dedicated customers; for hosted accounts key material is held in our KMS but we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for enterprise customers (BYOK) through our KMS integrations.

- Cross-border behavior: by default we keep execution in the requested country-region; during capacity constraints we route per policy but will not cross geopolitical regions for accounts that have region pinning enabled.

- Deletion timeline detail: explicit delete request -> immediate mark-for-deletion -> background worker purges transient caches within 0-6 hours; request traces and observability artifacts removed within 72 hours; archival provider deletion depends on their SLA (we initiate deletion and provide a signed confirmation once complete).

I've pasted a short, copyable paragraph below you can attach to your tracker:

"Redwood executes inference in the customer-specified region where possible. Ingress -> routing -> execution -> ephemeral caches -> short-term traces -> optional archival. Default retention: transient caches 0 days (evicted on use), request traces 7 days; on explicit deletion we purge caches within hours and traces within 72 hours; archival deletion initiated on request and confirmed after partner completion. For strict region constraints we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with account-level region pinning and BYOK options for additional control."
